kiriakou-on-greek-and-cypriot-food.summary: The experimental operation John Kiriakou paid for with a bank loan in September 2022, in which his stomach was removed to reverse an uncontrolled type 2 diabetes — a procedure he had found in a Lancet paper by a Scottish surgeon, and which cost him 55 kilos and, he says, the disease itself.

kiriakou-on-travel.title: Kiriakou on Greek and Cypriot food
kiriakou-on-travel.summary: The verdict John Kiriakou delivered on Cypriot cooking during a 2026 visit to the island — that its cheeses are more sophisticated and more distinct from one another than Greece's, where most are variations on a theme — together with his coffee positions, his conversion from frappé by a cousin in Rhodes, and his complaint about the size of the straw.

kiriakou-on-travel.title: Oman
kiriakou-on-travel.summary: The Gulf sultanate John Kiriakou singles out as America's most durable friend in the region and its most useful channel to Iran — a country that has acted as go-between for Washington and Tehran many times, and which he argues should be approached again in place of carrier deployments and public threats.

kiriakou-on-travel.title: John Kiriakou
kiriakou-on-travel.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

kiriakou-on-travel.title: Kiriakou's Cypriot ancestry
kiriakou-on-travel.summary: The DNA result showing John Kiriakou to be 24 per cent Cypriot — his largest single ancestry — which corrected a family belief that the line came from Crete and coincided with an invitation to address a Cypriot diaspora conference.

kiriakou-on-travel.title: There is no such thing as bad food in Athens
kiriakou-on-travel.summary: The lesson John Kiriakou says he learned at a lorry drivers' stop outside Corinth, where the food was as good as his grandmother's — reached on the three-and-a-half-hour drives he made to meet a source too sensitive to be met in Athens, with a vineyard tour as his cover story.

kiriakou-on-travel.title: Kiriakou on diet and nutrition
kiriakou-on-travel.summary: John Kiriakou''s views on eating, given to a Cypriot nutrition interviewer who challenged several of them: that the worst dietary advice he ever heard was to cut fat and cholesterol, that the American sugar lobby spent decades persuading the public that fat was the enemy, and that at his age carbohydrates are the enemy instead.

kiriakou-on-wine.title: John Kerry
kiriakou-on-wine.summary: U.S. Senator from Massachusetts; chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee during John Kiriakou's 2009 service as the committee's senior investigator; subsequently U.S. Secretary of State; characterized by Kiriakou as a coward who buckled under CIA pressure on the Dasht-i-Leili reopening and as personally fixated on his perceived theft of the Secretary of State position by Hillary Clinton; the famously thrown medals were duplicates purchased at the post exchange.

kiriakou-on-wine.title: John Brennan
kiriakou-on-wine.summary: Former Director of the CIA; characterized in KiriPedia's source corpus as the principal architect of the agency's enhanced interrogation program and as having plotted against an elected President

kiriakou-on-wine.title: AIPAC
kiriakou-on-wine.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee — the U.S. political organization that, in John Kiriakou's framing, ought to be registered as a foreign-lobbying entity but is not, and that wields decisive electoral power against U.S. elected officials who express support for Palestinian human rights.

kiriakou-on-wine.title: Brian Ross
kiriakou-on-wine.summary: American investigative journalist and seven-time Emmy Award winner who was a prominent reporter at ABC News when, in December 2007, he conducted the on-camera interview with John Kiriakou that produced the first public confirmation by a U.S. official that the CIA waterboarded prisoners. Per Kiriakou, Ross called him out of the blue with the assertion that a source said Kiriakou had personally tortured Abu Zubaydah; Kiriakou's decision to give the interview anyway — driven by the conclusion that 'Brian Ross's source is at the White House and they're going to pin this on me' — became the pivot point of his entire post-CIA life.

kiriakou-on-wine.title: Joe Biden
kiriakou-on-wine.summary: 46th President of the United States; Vice President during the first Obama term; at John Kerry's December 2009 Christmas party, recognized John Kiriakou from a 15-year-prior conversation about a mutual hometown friend, and openly told a Kiriakou colleague within Kiriakou's hearing — and across the room from Kerry — that he disliked the colleague.

kiriakou-on-wine.title: Kiriakou's transfer to the Directorate of Operations
kiriakou-on-wine.summary: John Kiriakou's roughly two-month internal campaign to transfer from the CIA's analytic Directorate of Intelligence to the operational Directorate of Operations, overcoming what he calls a "natural bias in operations against the eggheads on the analytic side," followed by an Athens posting secured because he was the only person in the entire CIA fluent in both Greek and Arabic. Covers his full CIA career arc from 1988/1990 recruitment through analyst years on Iraq, the switch to operations, 9/11, the enhanced-interrogation refusal, executive assistant to the deputy director for operations, and his eventual resignation and post-CIA career.

kiriakou-operational-eating.title: Kiriakou on diet and nutrition
kiriakou-operational-eating.summary: John Kiriakou''s views on eating, given to a Cypriot nutrition interviewer who challenged several of them: that the worst dietary advice he ever heard was to cut fat and cholesterol, that the American sugar lobby spent decades persuading the public that fat was the enemy, and that at his age carbohydrates are the enemy instead.

kiriakou-operational-eating.title: Kiriakou on Greek and Cypriot food
kiriakou-operational-eating.summary: The verdict John Kiriakou delivered on Cypriot cooking during a 2026 visit to the island — that its cheeses are more sophisticated and more distinct from one another than Greece's, where most are variations on a theme — together with his coffee positions, his conversion from frappé by a cousin in Rhodes, and his complaint about the size of the straw.

kiriakou-operational-eating.title: Kiriakou's Cypriot ancestry
kiriakou-operational-eating.summary: The DNA result showing John Kiriakou to be 24 per cent Cypriot — his largest single ancestry — which corrected a family belief that the line came from Crete and coincided with an invitation to address a Cypriot diaspora conference.

kiriakou-operational-eating.title: Kiriakou's gastrectomy
kiriakou-operational-eating.summary: The experimental operation John Kiriakou paid for with a bank loan in September 2022, in which his stomach was removed to reverse an uncontrolled type 2 diabetes — a procedure he had found in a Lancet paper by a Scottish surgeon, and which cost him 55 kilos and, he says, the disease itself.

kiriakou-operational-eating.title: Kiriakou on travel
kiriakou-operational-eating.summary: John Kiriakou''s own ranking of the countries he has visited: Greece his favourite and, he insists, the best food anywhere; Oman the most beautiful landscape; Syria the most extraordinary civilisation; and Chile the cheapest, illustrated by a bottle of a vineyard''s locked-away reserve that cost $8.50 on his honeymoon.

kiriakou-operational-eating.title: Kiriakou's type 2 diabetes
kiriakou-operational-eating.summary: The disease John Kiriakou was diagnosed with after leaving the CIA for a desk job, which he first fought down with a nutritionist's diet and a 70-pound weight loss, then lost ground to when insulin slowed his metabolism to a halt — reaching an A1C of 12.1 before he had his stomach removed to end it.

kiriakou-pardon-request.title: John Kiriakou
kiriakou-pardon-request.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

kiriakou-pardon-request.title: John Brennan
kiriakou-pardon-request.summary: Former Director of the CIA; characterized in KiriPedia's source corpus as the principal architect of the agency's enhanced interrogation program and as having plotted against an elected President

kiriakou-pardon-request.title: Donald Trump
kiriakou-pardon-request.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

kiriakou-pardon-request.title: Mar-a-Lago pardon pitch
kiriakou-pardon-request.summary: The lunch at which John Kiriakou put his pardon request directly to Donald Trump. Flown to Palm Beach by a wealthy friend who also wanted a pardon, Kiriakou delivered a prepared line as the president worked the dining room, was told to take it to Pam Bondi, and was afterwards vouched for on a speakerphone call to Trump by a political fixer who then asked him for $25,000 a month until the pardon came through.

kiriakou-pardon-request.title: "It''s either him or it''s Manning"
kiriakou-pardon-request.summary: John Kiriakou's account of why Barack Obama commuted Chelsea Manning's sentence — that Joe Biden, lobbied by a wealthy Greek-American businessman, argued Kiriakou's clemency case to the president directly, and that Obama cut the discussion off ten minutes in by saying he would do one or the other but not both. Kiriakou's conclusion is that the commutation was an arithmetic judgement about a 35-year sentence rather than an act of conscience.

kiriakou-pardon-request.title: The lawfare template
kiriakou-pardon-request.summary: The assessment of John Kiriakou''s prosecution that he quotes most often and finds most alarming: a former United States attorney for Utah told him the Kiriakou case was the template for the Democratic Party''s policy of lawfare. Kiriakou''s gloss is that if they do not like you they can ruin your life, and there is nothing you can do to protect yourself.

kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.title: The TikTok fan edits
kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.summary: The short-form videos made by a University of Texas sophomore, giving John Kiriakou a chipmunk voice and laser eyes, which reached Gen Z at scale and led within weeks to representation by a major talent agency and meetings about film and television.

kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.title: Abu Zubaydah
kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.title: Bureau of Prisons advisory board
kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.summary: The advisory board John Kiriakou joined at the personal invitation of the Director of the Bureau of Prisons, who told him the president had tasked him with tearing the Bureau down and rebuilding it.

kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.title: The Green Line in Nicosia
kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.summary: The division of Nicosia between the Republic of Cyprus and the Turkish-occupied north, which John Kiriakou toured in July 2026 and described as maintained through deliberate humiliation rather than any interest in settlement.

kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.title: Diary of a CEO — January 2026 Kiriakou interview
kiriakou-podcast-breakthrough.summary: The January 2026 long-form appearance by John Kiriakou on Steven Bartlett's Diary of a CEO podcast that a University of Texas at Austin sophomore then cut into TikTok shorts — sped and slowed, with lasers added — kicking off the Gen Z discovery of Kiriakou that pushed his cameo requests past 1,900 and drew a 2:30 a.m. representation call in Dubai from the Creative Artists Agency; Kiriakou treats it as the pivot after which stories he had been telling for nineteen years finally landed.

kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.title: Kiriakou's gastrectomy
kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.summary: The experimental operation John Kiriakou paid for with a bank loan in September 2022, in which his stomach was removed to reverse an uncontrolled type 2 diabetes — a procedure he had found in a Lancet paper by a Scottish surgeon, and which cost him 55 kilos and, he says, the disease itself.

kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.title: Kiriakou's type 2 diabetes
kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.summary: The disease John Kiriakou was diagnosed with after leaving the CIA for a desk job, which he first fought down with a nutritionist's diet and a 70-pound weight loss, then lost ground to when insulin slowed his metabolism to a halt — reaching an A1C of 12.1 before he had his stomach removed to end it.

kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.title: John Kiriakou
kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.title: The glyburide incident
kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.summary: The episode John Kiriakou described in a Letter from Loretto of 12 September 2014: handed a bottle of glyburide by the prison pharmacy without explanation, he crashed twice and passed out on the floor — and his physician father-in-law told him the drug could have put him into heart failure.

kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.title: Kiriakou on diet and nutrition
kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.summary: John Kiriakou''s views on eating, given to a Cypriot nutrition interviewer who challenged several of them: that the worst dietary advice he ever heard was to cut fat and cholesterol, that the American sugar lobby spent decades persuading the public that fat was the enemy, and that at his age carbohydrates are the enemy instead.

kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.title: Cofer Black
kiriakou-post-gastrectomy-complications.summary: Former head of the CIA Counterterrorism Center during and immediately after the September 11 attacks; principal architect of the agency's paramilitary turn on September 12, 2001; later Vice President of Blackwater under Erik Prince.

kiriakou-prison-designation.title: Bureau of Prisons
kiriakou-prison-designation.summary: The federal agency that ran John Kiriakou's incarceration — and one of his most persistent post-prison targets. The BOP overrode his judge's camp recommendation by deeming him "a threat to the public safety," threatened him with "diesel therapy" until 1,600 logged phone calls and letters from a dozen House members and two senators backed it off, and, per Kiriakou, functions as "an employment agency for unemployable semi-literate rural white men" and "a dumping ground for failed medical professionals" — an agency for which a prisoner's death is cheaper than his treatment.

kiriakou-prison-designation.title: FCI Loretto
kiriakou-prison-designation.summary: U.S. Federal Correctional Institution in Loretto, Pennsylvania; the low-medium-security prison at which John Kiriakou served 23 months of a 30-month sentence following his 2013 Espionage Act–era plea deal; the originally ordered "minimum security work camp" placement was countermanded — per Kiriakou, on Brennan's direct intervention — to place him in the actual prison alongside the general population.

kiriakou-prison-designation.title: Ghislaine Maxwell
kiriakou-prison-designation.summary: British socialite and convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, her father Robert Maxwell was a prolific Mossad spy, and she is the likely conduit through whom Jeffrey Epstein was introduced to and recruited by Mossad.

kiriakou-prison-designation.title: Julian Assange
kiriakou-prison-designation.summary: Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.

kiriakou-prison-designation.title: Jeffrey Epstein
kiriakou-prison-designation.summary: Convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, was "an Israeli access agent" rather than a CIA asset, because the CIA collects foreign intelligence and Epstein's targets — Bill Clinton, Bill Gates, Prince Andrew — were not foreign. Kiriakou further holds that Epstein did die by suicide in federal custody, because in the Bureau of Prisons the cameras never work and the guards are always asleep.

kiriakou-prison-designation.title: Brad Birkenfeld
kiriakou-prison-designation.summary: The UBS banking whistleblower, who was prosecuted and imprisoned before winning a $104 million settlement from the Treasury Department and spending it on the legal defence of other whistleblowers. John Kiriakou uses him as the measure of the gap between financial and national-security whistleblowing, and names him among the visitors whose devices he believes were copied at the Ecuadorian embassy in London.

kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.title: Prison racial segregation
kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the rigid racial and ethnic division of American prisons — a cafeteria split like the 1950s South — and his argument that segregating and hardening inmates for years, then releasing them with no skills, makes society less safe.

kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.title: Abraham Accords
kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.summary: The Trump-brokered normalization deals between Israel and Gulf Arab states — in John Kiriakou's judgment "a terrible idea in the first place," a great victory for Israel and the Gulf Arabs that was "a punch in the throat to the Palestinians." He argues the Accords are how Trump meant to "solve the Middle East in a day" — by screwing the Palestinians — that Hamas read the abandonment correctly, that October 7 shattered the project, and that reviving the Accords (Saudis in, victory declared, Nobel collected) remains the organizing goal of Trump's regional policy.

kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.title: Alan Dershowitz
kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.summary: American attorney and Harvard Law professor; John Kiriakou describes debating him on Piers Morgan's show over Jeffrey Epstein, telling Dershowitz he would have wanted to see him "hanging from a tree" had he sought leniency for Epstein as an Israeli spy — and cites attorney David Boies's on-air statement that Dershowitz was far more than Epstein's lawyer, also serving as his publicist, friend, and a guest on Epstein's island.

kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.title: Arianna Huffington
kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.summary: Founder of the Huffington Post and the accidental amplifier who turned John Kiriakou's prison writing into a phenomenon. His first Letter from Loretto went to his attorney, then to a friend running Firedoglake who — unknown to Kiriakou — was close to Huffington; she plastered it as a banner headline and it drew over a million hits, bringing CNN and 60 Minutes to the prison gates. She published his open letter to Snowden, ran the diesel-therapy exposé that triggered the "hands off John Kiriakou" campaign, and came to Loretto herself with two young journalists.

kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.title: Arrais Corporation
kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.summary: Private intelligence firm; companion entity to The Analysis Corporation; originally an LLC pass-through for retired Senior Intelligence Service personnel from the CIA's operations side; subsequently acquired by IBM for over $1 billion.

kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.title: Asset acquisition cycle
kiriakou-prison-manipulation-tactics.summary: The four-step process — spot, assess, develop, recruit — taught as the first lesson of CIA case officer training

kiriakou-public-speaking-training.title: Kiriakou's writing process
kiriakou-public-speaking-training.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of how he actually writes — books in waves over roughly nine months, op-eds in forty-five minutes to an hour once an idea has sat for a few days, and a habit of getting up at two in the morning to write one because he cannot sleep. He wrote *Remains of the Day* in six weeks during COVID, losing whole evenings to it: "I look at the clock again, it''s 2:00 in the morning. I''m like, oh my god, what happened?"

kiriakou-public-speaking-training.title: Admiral William Crowe
kiriakou-public-speaking-training.summary: Former Chairman of the U.S. Joint Chiefs of Staff and former CENTCOM commander who had lived in Bahrain, author of the "pound for pound" formula every Bahraini and every American ambassador quotes, and the visiting dignitary John Kiriakou was assigned to escort — a week that ended with the Bahraini Prime Minister refusing to let go of Kiriakou's hand.

kiriakou-public-speaking-training.title: Bahrain Posting (1994–1996)
kiriakou-public-speaking-training.summary: John Kiriakou's 1994–1996 assignment to Bahrain under U.S. State Department cover as second secretary for economic affairs — arriving with his wife Joanne and infant son Chris on August 1, 1994, into a tiny Gulf monarchy whose sectarian tensions erupted, two months later, into the first Intifada.

kiriakou-public-speaking-training.title: Global Response Staff
kiriakou-public-speaking-training.summary: The CIA's protective-security program for case officers operating in high-threat environments; run for the agency by Blackwater; especially active in Baghdad's Green Zone during the Iraq War, where movement between fixed locations was treated as life-threatening.

kiriakou-public-speaking-training.title: Hawala system
kiriakou-public-speaking-training.summary: Informal, ledger-based money-transfer network used across the Middle East, South Asia, and their diasporas to move funds without involving banks; per John Kiriakou's first-person account of testing one in the UAE — handing $50 to a grocer for a 16-digit number to redeem at an Arabic bakery in Bethesda, Maryland — completely untraceable; identified by Kiriakou (later, as Chief Investigator on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee) as one of the principal channels through which al-Qaeda moved operational money in the post-9/11 period, along with DHL.

kiriakou-public-speaking-training.title: John Walker Lindh
kiriakou-public-speaking-training.summary: American citizen captured while fighting alongside the Taliban in late 2001, present at the Qala-i-Jangi fortress at the start of the prisoner uprising that killed CIA officer Mike Spann. In John Kiriakou's account his case matters less for what Lindh did than for what was done around him — the false claim that he had been read his rights, the destruction of the career of the Justice Department lawyer who said so, and his place on the docket of the one judge who reserves national-security cases for herself.

kiriakou-russian-media.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
kiriakou-russian-media.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

kiriakou-russian-media.title: Julian Assange
kiriakou-russian-media.summary: Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.

kiriakou-russian-media.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
kiriakou-russian-media.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

kiriakou-russian-media.title: Russia-Ukraine war origins
kiriakou-russian-media.summary: John Kiriakou's account that the war began in 2014, not 2022 — rooted in broken U.S. promises that NATO would not expand to Russia's borders, the 2014 removal of a pro-Russian Ukrainian leader, and the seizure of Crimea; he says Russia is now winning and has no reason to negotiate.

kiriakou-russian-media.title: Maria Butina
kiriakou-russian-media.summary: Russian gun-rights activist convicted in the United States of failing to register as a foreign agent; John Kiriakou cites her case as an example of the "process crime" of FARA violations, contrasting the severity of her 18-month solitary-confinement sentence with federal guidelines calling for 0-6 months.

kiriakou-russian-media.title: NewsGuard
kiriakou-russian-media.summary: A media-rating organization, founded by the former head of Court TV and a former Wall Street Journal publisher, that scores news outlets 0-100 for reliability. Per John Kiriakou, NewsGuard docks any outlet that takes a position on Ukraine or Syria contrary to its preferred line, is subscribed to mostly by government entities (chiefly the Pentagon), and singled out Consortium News, the Grayzone, Antiwar.com, and ScheerPost over their criticism of U.S. policy — prompting a First Amendment lawsuit.

kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.title: Abolish the CIA
kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.summary: John Kiriakou's position that the CIA should be abolished because its functions are already duplicated by the other 17 U.S. intelligence agencies — analysis by the State Department, human spying by the Pentagon, technology by DARPA, NSA and the private sector.

kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.title: The CIA Insider's Guide to Surveillance and Surveillance Detection
kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.summary: Book by John Kiriakou drawing on his experience as a surveillance detection instructor at the CIA and as a private surveillance training consultant. The book covers the techniques used by intelligence professionals to identify whether they are being followed — including the four-phase surveillance detection route, concealment device placement and retrieval, and counter-surveillance strategy — adapted for use by corporate executives, journalists, and others who want to confirm whether they are being followed.

kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.title: FCI Loretto
kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.summary: U.S. Federal Correctional Institution in Loretto, Pennsylvania; the low-medium-security prison at which John Kiriakou served 23 months of a 30-month sentence following his 2013 Espionage Act–era plea deal; the originally ordered "minimum security work camp" placement was countermanded — per Kiriakou, on Brennan's direct intervention — to place him in the actual prison alongside the general population.

kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.title: Hunter Biden Laptop
kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment of the Hunter Biden laptop controversy — he saw nothing related to child sex abuse in the material but says the Biden family, particularly Hunter, has serious documented substance-abuse problems; and that the 2020 open letter in which 51 former intelligence officials called the story a Russian/KGB-style operation used deliberately hedged, CIA-trained language and was later shown (per Michael Morell's testimony) to have been solicited by the Biden campaign.

kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.title: Imran Khan
kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.summary: Former Prime Minister of Pakistan; subsequently deposed and imprisoned; his political party, the PTI (Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf), sent John Kiriakou a formal demand for apology after a November 2025 Indian-media interview in which Kiriakou observed that India would prevail over Pakistan in a conventional conflict; Kiriakou's reply has not been transcribed in polite company.

kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.title: J. Edgar Hoover
kiriakou-serial-killer-letters.summary: The FBI's founding director — 48 years in the chair — whose opposition nearly strangled the CIA at birth. Per John Kiriakou, Truman lifted Hoover's objection to the National Security Act of 1947 by disingenuously assuring him the CIA would be a division of the FBI; the lie seeded the two agencies' permanent mutual hatred. Kiriakou also credits Hoover with perfecting the annual ritual the CIA later copied — scaring Congress witless and demanding budget increases — and with controlling Hollywood's FBI image so tightly that no film could be made without his approval.

kiriakou-shortwave-listening.title: One-Time Pad
kiriakou-shortwave-listening.summary: Cipher system in which a secret, random key — shared between sender and receiver — is used to encode a message and then destroyed so that it can never be used again. In traditional shortwave-radio tradecraft, one-time pads enabled spies to broadcast number sequences over public airwaves that only the intended recipient, holding the matching page, could decode. Per John Kiriakou, his lifelong interest in intelligence began at age nine after he picked up KGB number transmissions on a 50-cent shortwave radio.

kiriakou-shortwave-listening.title: John Kiriakou
kiriakou-shortwave-listening.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

kiriakou-shortwave-listening.title: The scholar-in-residence pipeline
kiriakou-shortwave-listening.summary: John Kiriakou's description of retired CIA operations officers taking scholar-in-residence posts at universities and teaching literature courses that function, by their own account, as a recruitment funnel — students enrol knowing the instructor is a former officer and hoping for help getting in.

kiriakou-shortwave-listening.title: John le Carré
kiriakou-shortwave-listening.summary: British novelist and former MI6 officer, the subject of a full episode of John Kiriakou's Dead Drop podcast. Kiriakou's argument is that le Carré is the only spy novelist to have changed the business of spying itself — supplying its working vocabulary, from 'Joes' and 'lamplighters' to 'honey trap', and shaping how officers understood their own world.

kiriakou-shortwave-listening.title: Larry Devlin
kiriakou-shortwave-listening.summary: CIA officer and former chief of station in the Congo, whose memoir Chief of Station, Congo was published on his instruction the day after he died — never submitted to the agency's Publications Review Board. John Kiriakou cites it as an act of nerve he admits he does not have.

kiriakou-shortwave-listening.title: Publications Review Board
kiriakou-shortwave-listening.summary: The CIA office that must clear anything a former officer publishes. John Kiriakou says everything he writes goes to it — books, articles, "even a letter to the editor of Home and Garden magazine" — and describes how the turnaround tracked his standing at the agency: his first book took 22 months to clear while the leadership hated him; his most recent six cleared in days.

kiriakou-situational-awareness.title: The Islamabad surveillance incident
kiriakou-situational-awareness.summary: The episode in which John Kiriakou, then the CIA's chief of counterterrorism operations in Pakistan, detected a motorcyclist following him, resolved to kill the man, and discovered on a passing impulse that the surveillance was friendly.

kiriakou-situational-awareness.title: The CIA Insider's Guide to Surveillance and Surveillance Detection
kiriakou-situational-awareness.summary: Book by John Kiriakou drawing on his experience as a surveillance detection instructor at the CIA and as a private surveillance training consultant. The book covers the techniques used by intelligence professionals to identify whether they are being followed — including the four-phase surveillance detection route, concealment device placement and retrieval, and counter-surveillance strategy — adapted for use by corporate executives, journalists, and others who want to confirm whether they are being followed.

kiriakou-situational-awareness.title: Surveillance detection route
kiriakou-situational-awareness.summary: Tradecraft technique used by intelligence officers and assets to determine whether they are being followed before, during, or after an operational meeting

kiriakou-situational-awareness.title: Threats against John Kiriakou
kiriakou-situational-awareness.summary: The stalkers and death threats John Kiriakou has received since going public in 2007 — including a woman who believed he had proposed to her in code on C-SPAN and arrived at his office armed, and a caller who recited his son's home address.

kiriakou-situational-awareness.title: Kiriakou's television pilots
kiriakou-situational-awareness.summary: The eight television pilots John Kiriakou has sold over fifteen years as a hobby, beginning with Bomb Squad, a procedural about the New York City bomb squad built around a statistic that almost no bomb threat has anything to do with terrorism.

kiriakou-situational-awareness.title: Dead Drop (podcast)
kiriakou-situational-awareness.summary: John Kiriakou''s narrative podcast, launched in late 2025 — a season-long, memoir-style retelling of his life in intelligence, from recruitment ("The New Recruit") through Athens ("Golden Boy") to the post-9/11 hunt ("The Hunt Begins"), with mini-episodes like "A Spy''s Guide to Sofia." Written by Kiriakou with Alan Katz, produced by Costard & Touchstone Productions, with Kiriakou, Katz, and Nick Mechanic as executive producers. Its stated goal: "the deepest possible perspective on the world of spying and what makes any spy tick."

kiriakou-skeet-shooting.title: The shooting house
kiriakou-skeet-shooting.summary: The live-fire decision course at the Farm where a trainee has about three quarters of a second to decide whether the figure at the window is a gunman or a woman holding a baby — and where John Kiriakou says he never missed, which he connects to his own account of the temperament the CIA selects for.

kiriakou-skeet-shooting.title: The Farm
kiriakou-skeet-shooting.summary: The CIA's clandestine training facility in Virginia; site of approximately 80% of all CIA operational training

kiriakou-skeet-shooting.title: Counterterrorist driving
kiriakou-skeet-shooting.summary: The vehicle training at the Farm — the PIT manoeuvre and how to avoid one, when to ram a roadblock and where to hit it, reversing at sixty miles an hour — conducted in a fleet of junkyard beaters the CIA bought expressly to be wrecked.

kiriakou-skeet-shooting.title: The hostile border crossing exercise
kiriakou-skeet-shooting.summary: The training exercise run before dawn at a closed Dulles Airport in which CIA trainees crossed into the fictional Republic of Victoria — where John Kiriakou talked his way past a US-government-branded pen in his pocket, and the class clown ended up stripped to his underwear.

kiriakou-skeet-shooting.title: The operations course graduation
kiriakou-skeet-shooting.summary: The end of CIA field training: a graduation ceremony at which the whole class wore full disguises for the photograph, and a certificate that is itself classified and therefore cannot be displayed — it stays in the officer''s personnel file.

kiriakou-skeet-shooting.title: The bomb course
kiriakou-skeet-shooting.summary: The week-long CIA explosives course at a facility in another state, where John Kiriakou learned to build a Molotov cocktail, then a detonator rig, then an ammonium nitrate bomb — his final exam, which put a van's transmission three hundred yards into the woods.

kiriakou-television-pilots.title: Surveillance detection route
kiriakou-television-pilots.summary: Tradecraft technique used by intelligence officers and assets to determine whether they are being followed before, during, or after an operational meeting

kiriakou-television-pilots.title: Situational awareness
kiriakou-television-pilots.summary: The discipline John Kiriakou describes as the civilian version of surveillance detection — get out of the kill zone at the first sign of trouble, keep an escape route, and refuse to let the brain rationalise away what it is seeing.

kiriakou-television-pilots.title: Threats against John Kiriakou
kiriakou-television-pilots.summary: The stalkers and death threats John Kiriakou has received since going public in 2007 — including a woman who believed he had proposed to her in code on C-SPAN and arrived at his office armed, and a caller who recited his son's home address.

kiriakou-television-pilots.title: The Islamabad surveillance incident
kiriakou-television-pilots.summary: The episode in which John Kiriakou, then the CIA's chief of counterterrorism operations in Pakistan, detected a motorcyclist following him, resolved to kill the man, and discovered on a passing impulse that the surveillance was friendly.

kiriakou-television-pilots.title: Abu Zubaydah
kiriakou-television-pilots.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

kiriakou-television-pilots.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
kiriakou-television-pilots.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.title: Kiriakou's podcast breakthrough
kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.summary: The sequence by which John Kiriakou went from saying yes to every podcast request, including from teenagers, to appearances with the largest hosts in the world — a rise he attributes to three friends' shows triggering an algorithm in October 2024.

kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.title: John Kiriakou's Briefing Room
kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.summary: A twice-weekly news and commentary programme launched by John Kiriakou in July 2026, presented as analysis rather than partisan opinion, and distinct from his storytelling podcast Dead Drop.

kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.title: John Kiriakou
kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.title: 2026 Iran war
kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.title: Abraham Accords
kiriakou-tiktok-fan-edits.summary: The Trump-brokered normalization deals between Israel and Gulf Arab states — in John Kiriakou's judgment "a terrible idea in the first place," a great victory for Israel and the Gulf Arabs that was "a punch in the throat to the Palestinians." He argues the Accords are how Trump meant to "solve the Middle East in a day" — by screwing the Palestinians — that Hamas read the abandonment correctly, that October 7 shattered the project, and that reviving the Accords (Saudis in, victory declared, Nobel collected) remains the organizing goal of Trump's regional policy.

kiriakou-titanium-knee.title: Counterterrorist driving
kiriakou-titanium-knee.summary: The vehicle training at the Farm — the PIT manoeuvre and how to avoid one, when to ram a roadblock and where to hit it, reversing at sixty miles an hour — conducted in a fleet of junkyard beaters the CIA bought expressly to be wrecked.

kiriakou-titanium-knee.title: The operations course graduation
