tony-blinken.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

tony-blinken.title: Afghan heroin policy
tony-blinken.summary: The post-2001 U.S. policy in Afghanistan of protecting, and per John Kiriakou actively encouraging, the cultivation of heroin poppy. Under the Taliban in 2000 Afghanistan produced 0% of the world's heroin; by 2009 under American occupation it produced 93%. Per a DEA officer Kiriakou consulted with on the policy paper he was preparing for Senator Kerry, the strategic rationale was that nearly all of the heroin flowed to Iran and Russia, addiction in those countries was considered desirable as a long-run societal weakener, and the same logic now operates in reverse with Chinese fentanyl flowing into the United States.

tony-blinken.title: John Kerry
tony-blinken.summary: U.S. Senator from Massachusetts; chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee during John Kiriakou's 2009 service as the committee's senior investigator; subsequently U.S. Secretary of State; characterized by Kiriakou as a coward who buckled under CIA pressure on the Dasht-i-Leili reopening and as personally fixated on his perceived theft of the Secretary of State position by Hillary Clinton; the famously thrown medals were duplicates purchased at the post exchange.

tony-blinken.title: Bahrain Posting (1994–1996)
tony-blinken.summary: John Kiriakou's 1994–1996 assignment to Bahrain under U.S. State Department cover as second secretary for economic affairs — arriving with his wife Joanne and infant son Chris on August 1, 1994, into a tiny Gulf monarchy whose sectarian tensions erupted, two months later, into the first Intifada.

tony-blinken.title: China as economic threat
tony-blinken.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that China is the real threat to the West not militarily — it has one aircraft carrier to America's two dozen and rarely invades — but economically, buying friends worldwide while the U.S. spends a trillion dollars a year on weapons.

tony-mendez.title: Spy films and television on screen
tony-mendez.summary: John Kiriakou's scene-by-scene verdicts on how spy films and television handle real tradecraft — what they get right (static surveillance from upper floors, hostile operational meetings, exchanges of bona fides, breaking into offices), what they invent (silent helicopters, high-speed submersibles, Batcaves, gadgets that cannot be bought), and the shows he says commit felonies on screen. He opens with why CIA officers watch them at all — *"not because they love the CIA movies, but because they love to criticize them."*

tony-mendez.title: Bill Buckley
tony-mendez.summary: CIA station chief in Beirut kidnapped by Palestinian Islamic Jihad in March 1984; tortured at length over fifteen months; killed in captivity; the case from which the agency derived a generation of operational-security lessons including the abandonment of single-point tracking devices in CIA officers' personal kit.

tony-mendez.title: Zero Dark Thirty
tony-mendez.summary: 2012 film dramatizing the CIA hunt for Osama bin Laden, criticized on release for suggesting torture produced the intelligence that led to his capture. John Kiriakou surveys the mixed critical reception — praise from Time and the New Yorker for its craft, condemnation from journalist Michael Wolff and director Kathryn Bigelow's critics for what they called pro-torture propaganda — and notes his friend Senator John McCain said the film left him "sick... because it is wrong."

tony-mendez.title: Burn Notice
tony-mendez.summary: The USA Network spy series John Kiriakou watched as a fan before he became its script adviser — a job he obtained by sitting next to its creator, Matt Nix, on a flight from Washington to Los Angeles, having previously run the show's credits in slow motion to find out who was advising it. Nobody was. By the time the plane landed Kiriakou had the job for season six.

tony-mendez.title: CIA driving training
tony-mendez.summary: The counterterrorism-driving component of CIA training, in which officers are ambushed in a simulated third-country no-man's-land and must "get off the X" — get out of the kill zone. John Kiriakou's own run ended with the instructors killing his engine by remote, a robot in a van firing paintballs at him, and Kiriakou shooting out his own car windows to get an angle on the robot. "Damn it, Kiriakou. That was the last decent car we had."

tony-mendez.title: CIA psychological evaluations
tony-mendez.summary: The recurring psychiatric screening every CIA officer undergoes — before employment, again three years after hiring, and every five years thereafter for life, with extra sessions triggered by bad behaviour overseas. Per John Kiriakou, failing one grounds an officer — a colleague who "went nuts" could not be sent on a post-9/11 mission, and Kiriakou was sent in his place.

tora-bora.title: Pakistan Station (2002)
tora-bora.summary: John Kiriakou's January 2002 arrival in Islamabad to become CIA chief of counterterrorism operations — a journey via London and Kuwait with lost luggage, a warning that steered him away from the soon-to-be-bombed Marriott, a skeleton counterterrorism branch of seven CIA retirees, and the raids that followed.

tora-bora.title: Central Intelligence Agency
tora-bora.summary: U.S. foreign intelligence service; John Kiriakou's employer from 1990 to 2004 and the central institution of KiriPedia

tora-bora.title: John Kiriakou
tora-bora.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

tora-bora.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
tora-bora.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

tora-bora.title: Abu Zubaydah
tora-bora.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

tora-bora.title: Jordanian al-Qaeda detainee
tora-bora.summary: The subject of John Kiriakou's first-ever interrogation in Pakistan — a Jordanian who had gone to Afghanistan to run an orphanage, joined al-Qaeda for its funding, and told the truth about his escape route because 'I'm your prisoner; what good would it do to lie?'

training-foreign-intelligence-services.title: The propane truck ruse
training-foreign-intelligence-services.summary: The improvised environmental emergency John Kiriakou staged to empty a Middle Eastern cul-de-sac so a CIA lock-picking team could search a captured Hezbollah organiser's house — after his liaison partners rejected a gas leak on the ground that the country had no underground gas lines.

training-foreign-intelligence-services.title: Double-Agent Capture
training-foreign-intelligence-services.summary: Clandestine operation in which an intelligence service, having identified a recruited agent as working simultaneously for a hostile service, arranges a controlled final meeting to apprehend the agent before the agent can carry out orders — which may include killing the handler. Per John Kiriakou, he ran one such operation in the Middle East in the early 2000s after an NSA analyst warned him that his agent had just been ordered to shoot him in the next meeting.

training-foreign-intelligence-services.title: The weapons cache map
training-foreign-intelligence-services.summary: The single sheet of paper found inside an otherwise empty gun safe in the Middle East — a childlike map marked with an X and written directions past a palm tree and a large rock, which led John Kiriakou's team to a desert bunker packed to the ceiling with Hezbollah's arsenal.

training-foreign-intelligence-services.title: The Greek community of Warren, Ohio
training-foreign-intelligence-services.summary: The Greek-American community John Kiriakou's mother and first wife both came from — overwhelmingly from the island of Chios, closely enough knit that his divorce started a fistfight in a coffee house between men who had never met him.

training-foreign-intelligence-services.title: John Kiriakou
training-foreign-intelligence-services.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

training-foreign-intelligence-services.title: The Tiffany stationery letter
training-foreign-intelligence-services.summary: The deliberately expensive note John Kiriakou wrote to his first wife on Tiffany & Co. stationery, telling her he was halving her child support on the advice of counsel — a tactic suggested by his divorce lawyer to force her to file, and which worked the next day.

training-to-kill.title: Arabic and Greek
training-to-kill.summary: The qualification John Kiriakou says opened the door to his transfer from CIA analysis to operations: he was, by his account, the only person in the agency fluent in both Arabic and Greek, at a moment when a counterterrorism position was open in Athens.

training-to-kill.title: Iraq, the training account
training-to-kill.summary: The reason John Kiriakou says he was given the Iraq portfolio as a new CIA analyst in 1990 — that nothing ever happened there — and the promise that once he had learned tradecraft and the house writing style he would be moved to somewhere exciting, such as Romania.

training-to-kill.title: The Powell telephone call
training-to-kill.summary: The morning call John Kiriakou says he took from General Colin Powell, then chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, asking who would have run an Iraqi operation to kill former President George H. W. Bush; Kiriakou named the Iraqi Intelligence Service station in Basra and its headquarters in Baghdad, and eight hours later the United States fired forty-eight cruise missiles at that building.

training-to-kill.title: Bankruptcy and the dropped charges
training-to-kill.summary: The sequence John Kiriakou places at the centre of his case: that the espionage counts against him were dropped only after his legal fees had bankrupted him, which he presents as evidence that the government''s aim was attrition rather than conviction.

training-to-kill.title: Curtailment cables
training-to-kill.summary: The career-ending requests John Kiriakou says he read coming back from the CIA's black sites — officers, doctors, psychologists and nurses asking to end their tours early rather than continue to take part in the interrogation programme — and his conclusion that if that many people were objecting in classified channels, someone would surely go public.

training-to-kill.title: "It''s about mitigating damage"
training-to-kill.summary: The sentence John Kiriakou credits with changing his mind about going to trial — one of his own attorneys telling him that his problem was that he thought the case was about justice, when it was about mitigating damage — and the two lawyers who drove to his house after he emailed at six in the morning to refuse the plea.

trilateral-commission.title: The Pentagon's congressional district strategy
trilateral-commission.summary: The practice John Kiriakou describes of placing defence manufacturing orders in effectively all 435 congressional districts, so that every member of Congress has constituents dependent on the defence budget — and nobody has an incentive to vote against it.

trilateral-commission.title: AIPAC
trilateral-commission.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee — the U.S. political organization that, in John Kiriakou's framing, ought to be registered as a foreign-lobbying entity but is not, and that wields decisive electoral power against U.S. elected officials who express support for Palestinian human rights.

trilateral-commission.title: Jeffrey Epstein
trilateral-commission.summary: Convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, was "an Israeli access agent" rather than a CIA asset, because the CIA collects foreign intelligence and Epstein's targets — Bill Clinton, Bill Gates, Prince Andrew — were not foreign. Kiriakou further holds that Epstein did die by suicide in federal custody, because in the Bureau of Prisons the cameras never work and the guards are always asleep.

trilateral-commission.title: 2026 Iran war
trilateral-commission.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

trilateral-commission.title: Adnan Khashoggi
trilateral-commission.summary: Saudi arms dealer and Iran-Contra middleman whom John Kiriakou says was mentioned 'all the time' at the CIA — in pointed contrast to Jeffrey Epstein, whose name he never once heard there.

trilateral-commission.title: Alexander Acosta and the sweetheart deal
trilateral-commission.summary: The US attorney who gave Jeffrey Epstein his 2006 non-prosecution agreement and later said he had been ordered to — a chain of command John Kiriakou traces upward to an attorney general famous for his powerlessness, and therefore to somebody above him whom nobody has ever named.

trita-parsi.title: Max Blumenthal
trita-parsi.summary: American investigative journalist and a personal friend of John Kiriakou, whom Kiriakou calls one of the most brilliant people he has ever encountered and singles out for an ability to assemble scattered fragments into a picture 'in a way that almost no one else I know is able to do.' Kiriakou also recounts Blumenthal's arrest outside the Venezuelan embassy, where he says video showed Blumenthal was the one assaulted, and counts him among the independent journalists under the same official pressure he is.

trita-parsi.title: MOSSAD
trita-parsi.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

trita-parsi.title: Iran Nuclear Assessment
trita-parsi.summary: Per John Kiriakou's assessment, the US–Israeli military campaign against Iran was a war of choice driven by Israeli political pressure rather than genuine intelligence indicating an Iranian nuclear weapons threat. The CIA produced two National Intelligence Estimates concluding Iran had no nuclear weapons program; Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khamenei issued a fatwa in the 1980s forbidding such a program. The U.S. went to war anyway, in Kiriakou's view, after President Trump replaced the Joint Chiefs of Staff with officers willing to accept Israeli intelligence and proceed.

trita-parsi.title: Nobel Peace Prize
trita-parsi.summary: The prize a Swedish parliamentarian nominated John Kiriakou for in 2016 — a marker of how far world opinion had swung his way after prison. Kiriakou once believed Obama deserved his; he came to see it as unearned, and he treats Trump's foreign policy as substantially organized around wanting one too — "never underestimate Donald Trump's desire to win a Nobel Peace Prize," a White House friend told him. Netanyahu's nomination of Trump he summarized in a single unprintable phrase.

trita-parsi.title: Iran 12-Day War
trita-parsi.summary: 2025 Israeli air campaign against Iran during which Israel killed at least fourteen Iranian nuclear scientists by destroying the apartment buildings they lived in; preceded for each scientist by Farsi-language telephone calls from Iranian-Jewish Mossad and Shin Bet officers offering defection in lieu of certain death; characterized by John Kiriakou as a categorical departure from CIA targeting doctrine in its acceptable-civilian-casualty calculus.

trita-parsi.title: Scott Horton
trita-parsi.summary: American antiwar journalist and interviewer whom John Kiriakou calls one of the most brilliant people he has ever engaged with on Middle East questions. The two appeared together on a Piers Morgan panel opposite Alan Dershowitz and a former Israeli intelligence chief, arguing that Israel spies actively on the United States.

truck-and-cat-in-the-hat.title: The Italians at Loretto
truck-and-cat-in-the-hat.summary: The mafia contingent at FCI Loretto — men with last names like Gambino, Bonanno, Lucchese, Genovese, DeCavalcante — who adopted John Kiriakou in his second year, largely because he hated the FBI as much as they did. The cast included the boss of the Gambino family (in on a dozen-plus murder counts, the man who replaced John Gotti), Pete the Bonanno captain across the hall who asked why he sat "with those Nazi retards," and a crooked guard on the payroll delivering pork loin and fresh mozzarella. When the FBI later came to Kiriakou's door asking him to inform on Pete, his answer was "get off my property."

truck-and-cat-in-the-hat.title: John Kiriakou
truck-and-cat-in-the-hat.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

truck-and-cat-in-the-hat.title: The Oz analogy
truck-and-cat-in-the-hat.summary: John Kiriakou's habit of explaining federal prison social structure through the HBO drama Oz, in which rival gangs are forced to share a single unit — and his identification with the show's unaffiliated Irish character, who belonged to no faction and survived by playing them off one another.

truck-and-cat-in-the-hat.title: 9/11 plea agreements
truck-and-cat-in-the-hat.summary: The Biden-era plea deals under which Khalid Sheikh Mohammed and co-defendants agreed to plead guilty to murdering 2,976 people in exchange for life without parole and a guarantee against transfer to the Colorado supermax — vacated by the Secretary of Defense after public backlash. Per John Kiriakou, the deals existed because torture had rendered every confession inadmissible, leaving no usable evidence.

truck-and-cat-in-the-hat.title: AIPAC and foreign-agent registration
truck-and-cat-in-the-hat.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that AIPAC is the only organization of its kind exempt from registering under the Foreign Agents Registration Act — set against his own experience around 2008, when a contract worth five or six thousand dollars to write four op-eds praising the Abu Dhabi Chamber of Commerce obliged him to register as a foreign agent.

truck-and-cat-in-the-hat.title: George McGovern
truck-and-cat-in-the-hat.summary: The 1972 Democratic presidential nominee, whose landslide defeat John Kiriakou identifies as the pretext for creating superdelegates. As a George Washington University sophomore in 1983, Kiriakou wrote to McGovern offering the campus theater for a campaign launch; McGovern telephoned him personally, announced his 1984 candidacy there, and afterwards took him home for tuna sandwiches made by his wife.

truck-the-serial-killer.title: Chomo
truck-the-serial-killer.summary: The prison term for a child molester, which John Kiriakou first heard on his first day at FCI Loretto when two skinheads at the Aryan table put it to him as the last of three vetting questions before deciding whether he could eat with them.

truck-the-serial-killer.title: FCI Loretto
truck-the-serial-killer.summary: U.S. Federal Correctional Institution in Loretto, Pennsylvania; the low-medium-security prison at which John Kiriakou served 23 months of a 30-month sentence following his 2013 Espionage Act–era plea deal; the originally ordered "minimum security work camp" placement was countermanded — per Kiriakou, on Brennan's direct intervention — to place him in the actual prison alongside the general population.

truck-the-serial-killer.title: Larry Raviv
truck-the-serial-killer.summary: Fellow federal prisoner of John Kiriakou, convicted of murder-for-hire after taking out a life insurance policy on his business partner to pay off a $100,000 mob gambling debt and hiring a hitman to kill him. Raviv negotiated a 20-year sentence, down from what would normally be life without parole, by testifying against the hitman, who died of a heart attack while awaiting extradition trial. Kiriakou later engineered a violent beating against Raviv after Raviv called him a "rat" for being summoned to the lieutenant's office for a Jake Tapper interview.

truck-the-serial-killer.title: Federal prison security levels
truck-the-serial-killer.summary: The ladder of federal custody as John Kiriakou describes it — penitentiary, medium, low and minimum-security camp — the transfer rules that let long-sentence prisoners descend it, and why that placed dangerous men inside the low-security prison where he served his sentence.

truck-the-serial-killer.title: Clint Goswick
truck-the-serial-killer.summary: Fellow federal prisoner of John Kiriakou at FCI Loretto; a devout Christian and Wichita Falls, Texas heating-and-air-conditioning business owner convicted of drug conspiracy and a gun charge despite never having used, possessed, manufactured, or distributed drugs.

truck-the-serial-killer.title: Doing Time Like a Spy
truck-the-serial-killer.summary: Prison memoir by John Kiriakou, full title Doing Time Like a Spy: How the CIA Taught Me to Survive and Thrive in Prison; winner of two literary awards and reissued in a second edition by Simon and Schuster.

truman-cia-op-ed.title: Gina Haspel
truman-cia-op-ed.summary: Director of the Central Intelligence Agency under President Trump's first term; known to John Kiriakou and others at the CIA as "Bloody Gina"; per Kiriakou, flew out to the secret black site to sit in on one of the enhanced-interrogation torture sessions "just because she could," personally supervised the torture of USS Cole bombing suspect Rahim al-Nashiri, and later fed the CIA's torture tapes into an industrial document grinder after being explicitly told by White House Counsel not to destroy them.

truman-cia-op-ed.title: Abolish the CIA
truman-cia-op-ed.summary: John Kiriakou's position that the CIA should be abolished because its functions are already duplicated by the other 17 U.S. intelligence agencies — analysis by the State Department, human spying by the Pentagon, technology by DARPA, NSA and the private sector.

truman-cia-op-ed.title: Central Intelligence Agency
truman-cia-op-ed.summary: U.S. foreign intelligence service; John Kiriakou's employer from 1990 to 2004 and the central institution of KiriPedia

truman-cia-op-ed.title: Founding of the CIA (1947)
truman-cia-op-ed.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the CIA's creation under the National Security Act of 1947 — built with British MI6 help after a chaotic 1945-47 interregnum, and opposed by J. Edgar Hoover until Truman falsely promised him the new agency would be part of the FBI.

truman-cia-op-ed.title: In-Q-Tel
truman-cia-op-ed.summary: The CIA's openly acknowledged venture capital arm; provided Palantir Technologies its first $1.5 million in seed funding; in John Kiriakou's account the principal vehicle by which the agency finances private-sector development of technologies it intends to use.

truman-cia-op-ed.title: Kiriakou's Cuba trip
truman-cia-op-ed.summary: John Kiriakou's account of his first visit to Cuba, where his books sit in the national library and officials treated him warmly — and a Cuban vice president told him every U.S. president is 'the same,' blaming Cuba while it cannot keep the lights on. He was invited as a guest of the Havana international book fair after his first two books were translated into Spanish, and later wrote about how the U.S. embargo shapes daily life there, from a dengue-fever hospital bill he had to pay in euros to a diet dominated by squash.

trump-cartel-terrorist-designation.title: Expanding the definition of terrorism
trump-cartel-terrorist-designation.summary: John Kiriakou's objection to the widening of the U.S. terrorism designation beyond groups that use violence for political ends — covering the addition of organisations loosely associated with Antifa, which he argues is not a group at all, and the designation of Latin American narco organisations, which he says should be answered with criminal charges rather than drone strikes.

trump-cartel-terrorist-designation.title: Anwar al-Awlaki
trump-cartel-terrorist-designation.summary: American-born al-Qaeda propagandist; in 1993 the imam of the Falls Church, Virginia mosque visited by John Kiriakou's CIA Arabic-language class on a field trip; in 2001 the cleric at whose mosque the 9/11 hijackers prayed the night before the attacks; killed by U.S. drone strike in Yemen in approximately 2011.

trump-cartel-terrorist-designation.title: Aafia Siddiqui
trump-cartel-terrorist-designation.summary: Pakistani-American scientist arrested in Afghanistan in 2008 and convicted in the U.S. of attempting to shoot two FBI agents; per John Kiriakou, who covered the arrest as a terrorism consultant for ABC News, newer evidence indicates she never had a gun and never fired at anyone, and her claim that the CIA seized her three children at arrest has never been resolved for the youngest, who would now be 18.

trump-cartel-terrorist-designation.title: Abu Zubaydah
trump-cartel-terrorist-designation.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

trump-cartel-terrorist-designation.title: Advanced Counterterrorism Operations
trump-cartel-terrorist-designation.summary: The six-week specialist course John Kiriakou flew back from Athens to attend roughly eighteen months before 9/11 as one of fourteen officers selected worldwide — high-threat operations, technical collection, and a driving syllabus built around crashing through roadblocks that left the class with whiplash. By accident of timing it meant a trained cadre was ready to deploy the moment the attacks came.

trump-cartel-terrorist-designation.title: Asset acquisition cycle
trump-cartel-terrorist-designation.summary: The four-step process — spot, assess, develop, recruit — taught as the first lesson of CIA case officer training

trump-dni-replacement.title: Anwar al-Awlaki
trump-dni-replacement.summary: American-born al-Qaeda propagandist; in 1993 the imam of the Falls Church, Virginia mosque visited by John Kiriakou's CIA Arabic-language class on a field trip; in 2001 the cleric at whose mosque the 9/11 hijackers prayed the night before the attacks; killed by U.S. drone strike in Yemen in approximately 2011.

trump-dni-replacement.title: MOSSAD
trump-dni-replacement.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

trump-dni-replacement.title: Rand Paul Eric Holder
trump-dni-replacement.summary: Rand Paul asked whether the president may kill an American on US soil without trial. Kiriakou recounts Holder''s eventual answer: yes.

trump-dni-replacement.title: Tulsi Gabbard
trump-dni-replacement.summary: U.S. Director of National Intelligence; a longtime family friend of John Kiriakou's, who has known her since she was 12; Kiriakou calls her appointment "an inspired choice" despite disagreeing with her decision to join the Republican Party, and says she appears to have given up her opposition to Section 702 surveillance to secure Senate confirmation.

trump-dni-replacement.title: Alexa
trump-dni-replacement.summary: Per John Kiriakou, Amazon''s Alexa smart speaker reports directly to the NSA — and he owns one anyway. The device recurs across his interviews as the standing example of the surveillance trade-off in modern smart-home technology, and of his own negotiated exception to it: one speaker, in one room, against the advice of every intelligence officer he has ever known.

trump-dni-replacement.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
trump-dni-replacement.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

trump-glorification-and-the-iran-war.title: 2026 Iran war
trump-glorification-and-the-iran-war.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

trump-glorification-and-the-iran-war.title: Donald Trump
trump-glorification-and-the-iran-war.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

trump-glorification-and-the-iran-war.title: 2026 Iran war economic shock
trump-glorification-and-the-iran-war.summary: John Kiriakou''s running assessment of the economic damage from the 2026 Iran war — an oil shock he says already exceeds both 1970s shocks combined, a natural-gas shock worse than the Nord Stream destruction, and a chokepoint problem that runs through fertilizer as much as fuel, since 65% of the world''s supply must transit the Strait of Hormuz. His summary: "This is an economic slowdown of choice."

trump-glorification-and-the-iran-war.title: American missile stockpiles
trump-glorification-and-the-iran-war.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that the United States has run its interceptor stocks down to the point of strategic vulnerability — that the conventional wisdom in Washington was that a round of the Iran war ended because the Patriots ran out, and that a country which cannot fight a two-front war certainly cannot do it below maximum production.

trump-glorification-and-the-iran-war.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
trump-glorification-and-the-iran-war.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

trump-glorification-and-the-iran-war.title: Breaking the nuclear taboo
trump-glorification-and-the-iran-war.summary: John Kiriakou's reporting that Donald Trump considered using a tactical nuclear weapon in Iran not for military necessity but to break what he regards as warfare's final taboo, freeing future presidents to use larger weapons — and the related account that the chairman of the Joint Chiefs refused him the nuclear codes.

trump-iran-ceasefire-efforts.title: Donald Trump
trump-iran-ceasefire-efforts.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

trump-iran-ceasefire-efforts.title: Iran Nuclear Assessment
trump-iran-ceasefire-efforts.summary: Per John Kiriakou's assessment, the US–Israeli military campaign against Iran was a war of choice driven by Israeli political pressure rather than genuine intelligence indicating an Iranian nuclear weapons threat. The CIA produced two National Intelligence Estimates concluding Iran had no nuclear weapons program; Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khamenei issued a fatwa in the 1980s forbidding such a program. The U.S. went to war anyway, in Kiriakou's view, after President Trump replaced the Joint Chiefs of Staff with officers willing to accept Israeli intelligence and proceed.

trump-iran-ceasefire-efforts.title: Iran 12-Day War
trump-iran-ceasefire-efforts.summary: 2025 Israeli air campaign against Iran during which Israel killed at least fourteen Iranian nuclear scientists by destroying the apartment buildings they lived in; preceded for each scientist by Farsi-language telephone calls from Iranian-Jewish Mossad and Shin Bet officers offering defection in lieu of certain death; characterized by John Kiriakou as a categorical departure from CIA targeting doctrine in its acceptable-civilian-casualty calculus.

trump-iran-ceasefire-efforts.title: John McCain
trump-iran-ceasefire-efforts.summary: Late U.S. Senator from Arizona who gave the most consequential Senate-floor defense of John Kiriakou — declaring that 'if it weren't for John Kiriakou, the American people would never have had any idea what the CIA was doing in their name' — and sponsored the McCain–Feinstein amendment banning torture.

trump-iran-ceasefire-efforts.title: Marco Rubio
trump-iran-ceasefire-efforts.summary: U.S. official whom John Kiriakou identifies as the real motivator behind pressure on Venezuela; Kiriakou argues Venezuela is not a meaningful drug threat to the U.S. and that Rubio simply wants Maduro gone.

trump-iran-ceasefire-efforts.title: Mohsen Rafighdoost
trump-iran-ceasefire-efforts.summary: Iranian journalist and political figure whom John Kiriakou identifies as a co-founder of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and the propaganda voice behind the audio tapes distributed in Iran before the 1979 revolution; interviewed on the PBD Podcast, he conceded that the Shah's regime held only 3,000–3,500 political prisoners rather than the 100,000 opposition figures claimed at the time and that the Shah was, in his own judgment, a better man than Ayatollah Khomeini.

trump-tariffs.title: Donald Trump
trump-tariffs.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

trump-tariffs.title: Richard D. Wolff
trump-tariffs.summary: American Marxian economist, professor emeritus at the University of Massachusetts Amherst and a recurring guest of John Kiriakou, who calls him one of his favourite people and says he feels smarter after every conversation; Wolff's appearances supply Kiriakou's audience with a class analysis of tariffs, federal debt and the periodic crashes of capitalism.

trump-tariffs.title: Youngstown Sheet and Tube
trump-tariffs.summary: The Ohio steel producer whose closure John Kiriakou treats as the moment the economy of his hometown region ended; he remembers the day it shut and classmates weeping in the school hallways because their fathers had lost their jobs, and dates the collapse of New Castle, Pennsylvania to it.

trump-tariffs.title: China as economic threat
trump-tariffs.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that China is the real threat to the West not militarily — it has one aircraft carrier to America's two dozen and rarely invades — but economically, buying friends worldwide while the U.S. spends a trillion dollars a year on weapons.

trump-tariffs.title: John Kiriakou
trump-tariffs.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

trump-tariffs.title: Permanent wartime economy
trump-tariffs.summary: John Kiriakou's thesis that since 9/11 the United States has run a permanent wartime economy so large that cutting the defense budget would trigger a depression — likening the dependency to crack addiction and warning it makes war almost inevitable.

trump.title: Cofer Black
trump.summary: Former head of the CIA Counterterrorism Center during and immediately after the September 11 attacks; principal architect of the agency's paramilitary turn on September 12, 2001; later Vice President of Blackwater under Erik Prince.

trump.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
trump.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

trump.title: Chelsea Manning
trump.summary: Former U.S. Army intelligence analyst who provided WikiLeaks its 2010 trove of military and diplomatic documents. Per John Kiriakou, Manning meets the legal definition of whistleblower for exposing war crimes, was a torture victim of prolonged solitary confinement with forced nudity, and was sentenced to 35 years in prison before Barack Obama commuted — not pardoned — her sentence. Kiriakou says Manning later refused a grand jury's offer of immunity and chose renewed jail time rather than testify against Julian Assange.

trump.title: CIA–FBI interagency rivalry and 9/11
trump.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the historical CIA–FBI rivalry, dating to J. Edgar Hoover's opposition to the 1947 National Security Act, and how it manifested before September 11 when Cofer Black's Counterterrorism Center withheld from the FBI that hijackers Nawaf al-Hazmi and Khalid al-Mihdhar had been granted U.S. visas.

trump.title: Founding of the CIA (1947)
trump.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the CIA's creation under the National Security Act of 1947 — built with British MI6 help after a chaotic 1945-47 interregnum, and opposed by J. Edgar Hoover until Truman falsely promised him the new agency would be part of the FBI.

trump.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
trump.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

trumpcare-confusion.title: Progressive taxation
trumpcare-confusion.summary: John Kiriakou''s argument that the United States abandoned a system it was once proud of: taxation based, in Theodore Roosevelt''s formulation, on a person''s ability to pay. It fell apart under Ronald Reagan, he says, and the regressive substitutes now proposed — a higher gas tax among them — hit the people least able to absorb them.

trumpcare-confusion.title: The Speaker's office as gatekeeper
trumpcare-confusion.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of how legislative power moved in the mid-1990s from committee chairmen and the Rules Committee into the office of the Speaker of the House, where it has stayed because no subsequent Speaker has wanted to give it back — and the member of Congress who explained the death of his own whistleblower bill in four words: ''Nancy said I couldn''t.''

trumpcare-confusion.title: Lobbyists writing legislation
trumpcare-confusion.summary: John Kiriakou''s first-hand account from the Senate Foreign Relations Committee: told that the committee would take part in the carbon offsets debate and protesting that he knew nothing about carbon offsets, he was told not to worry — and the next day strangers came into the office, took over most of the desks, logged on and began writing the bill.

trumpcare-confusion.title: Think tank financing
trumpcare-confusion.summary: John Kiriakou's warning that Washington's think tanks — more than 1,200 of them by a Washington Post count — must be read through their funding, illustrated with the case of someone close to him who controlled about $200,000 a year in donations for a Fortune 100 defence contractor and moved the money when a household-name institute proved insufficiently pro-contractor.

trumpcare-confusion.title: Donald Trump
trumpcare-confusion.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

trumpcare-confusion.title: Trump tariffs
trumpcare-confusion.summary: The across-the-board tariffs imposed by Donald Trump on United States trading partners, which John Kiriakou describes as having shaken up the economy faster than any president in generations — causing chaos in global stock markets, laying the groundwork for inflation and economic contraction, and producing political upheaval at home.

tucker-carlson-2026-fara-referral.title: Tucker Carlson
tucker-carlson-2026-fara-referral.summary: American broadcaster and former Fox News host; a personal friend of John Kiriakou's for years, appearing on Kiriakou's radio and podcast work and hosting him roughly a dozen times on his own Fox show. Kiriakou calls him possibly the most brilliant and best-informed person he has ever encountered, and relays Glenn Greenwald's belief that Carlson could win the presidency — an idea Carlson privately dismisses.

tucker-carlson-2026-fara-referral.title: Abu Zubaydah
tucker-carlson-2026-fara-referral.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

tucker-carlson-2026-fara-referral.title: Daniel Ellsberg
tucker-carlson-2026-fara-referral.summary: The Pentagon Papers whistleblower Kiriakou calls 'the Godfather of all national security whistleblowers' — and one of the great mentors of his life.

tucker-carlson-2026-fara-referral.title: Jason Leopold
tucker-carlson-2026-fara-referral.summary: Bloomberg investigative journalist; characterized by John Kiriakou as the leading practitioner of Freedom of Information Act litigation against U.S. [intelligence agencies](/wiki/intelligence-agencies); broke the Hillary Clinton private-email-server story; whose FOIA suit against the CIA Office of Public Affairs produced documentary evidence that NBC's chief national-security correspondent had been sending articles to the CIA for clearance before sending them to his own editor.

tucker-carlson-2026-fara-referral.title: John Kiriakou
tucker-carlson-2026-fara-referral.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

tucker-carlson-2026-fara-referral.title: Ken Dilanian
tucker-carlson-2026-fara-referral.summary: Chief national-security correspondent at NBC News and MSNBC; documented — through a Jason Leopold Freedom of Information Act lawsuit against the CIA — to have sent his own articles to the CIA Office of Public Affairs for clearance before sending them to his own editor.

tucker-carlson.title: John Kiriakou
tucker-carlson.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

tucker-carlson.title: Candace Owens
tucker-carlson.summary: The commentator whose claims about the killing of Charlie Kirk John Kiriakou has publicly declined to accept. He credits her reach and her intelligence and rejects her method, citing an earlier occasion — a conference call he says he was on — at which she claimed irrefutable proof that the Italian government had stolen the 2020 election and that its release would return Donald Trump to office.

tucker-carlson.title: Charlie Kirk shooting
tucker-carlson.summary: Kiriakou questions the official account: a court filing says the ATF could not match the autopsy bullet to the rifle tied to the suspect.

tucker-carlson.title: Christian Zionism
tucker-carlson.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that American evangelical Christianity functions as an arm of Zionism, and that its support for Israel is helping extinguish the oldest Christian communities on earth — a position he says he argued directly with the evangelical students he was invited to teach, and which he grounds in the projection that Nazareth, Christian for two thousand years, may soon have no Christians left.

tucker-carlson.title: Donald Trump
tucker-carlson.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

tucker-carlson.title: Tucker Carlson 2026 FARA referral
tucker-carlson.summary: The March 2026 criminal referral against Tucker Carlson to the U.S. Department of Justice accusing him of treason, espionage and Foreign Agents Registration Act violations that John Kiriakou says was widely misattributed to the CIA before the pro-Israel political activist Laura Loomer publicly claimed authorship the following day; Kiriakou treats the episode as an escalation from Israeli-aligned political actors and warns Carlson to worry less about legal jeopardy than about physical safety.

tuesday-morning-kill-list.title: MOSSAD
tuesday-morning-kill-list.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

tuesday-morning-kill-list.title: Executive Order 12333
tuesday-morning-kill-list.summary: The U.S. presidential directive — in its post-9/11 amended form — that grants the CIA the legal authority to kill any individual anywhere in the world deemed by the agency to pose a "clear and present danger" to the United States; the legal foundation underlying both CIA paramilitary operations and the agency's contractor relationships including with Blackwater.

tuesday-morning-kill-list.title: Jeffrey Epstein
tuesday-morning-kill-list.summary: Convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, was "an Israeli access agent" rather than a CIA asset, because the CIA collects foreign intelligence and Epstein's targets — Bill Clinton, Bill Gates, Prince Andrew — were not foreign. Kiriakou further holds that Epstein did die by suicide in federal custody, because in the Bureau of Prisons the cameras never work and the guards are always asleep.

tuesday-morning-kill-list.title: CIA and NSA exotic programs
tuesday-morning-kill-list.summary: Two obscure U.S. intelligence programs John Kiriakou has discussed — a late-1980s FBI/Defense Department investigation into a senior NSA officer who came out as a member of the Church of Satan and was accused of ritual sacrifice (which found no evidence), and a 1990s CIA battlefield laser weapon designed to blind rather than kill enemy soldiers, shelved after lawyers determined it violated international law.

tuesday-morning-kill-list.title: Kathryn Ruemmler
tuesday-morning-kill-list.summary: Obama White House counsel whose Epstein-file emails show her repeatedly trying to introduce Jeffrey Epstein to CIA director John Brennan; John Kiriakou notes she personally received a rare CIA award from Brennan and, as the White House's top lawyer, would have been the final legal authority approving the Tuesday-morning kill list.

tuesday-morning-kill-list.title: Operation Midnight Climax
tuesday-morning-kill-list.summary: Sub-project of the CIA's MK-Ultra program, conducted in San Francisco. Per John Kiriakou, the CIA rented a safe house and paid sex workers to bring men back to it, where agents dosed the men with LSD without their knowledge or consent, then observed their behavior through one-way mirrors. The operation followed an earlier phase in which the CIA had dosed its own employees; when that produced suicides, it moved to using unconsenting members of the public.

tulsi-gabbard.title: MOSSAD
tulsi-gabbard.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

tulsi-gabbard.title: Decapitation strikes
tulsi-gabbard.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that killing an adversary's leadership does not defeat the adversary — grounded in a standing joke from his own service that the CIA had killed twenty-seven separate "number three" figures in al-Qaeda, and applied to the 2026 Iran war, where the entire political, military and scientific leadership was killed in the opening days and the fighting continued regardless.

tulsi-gabbard.title: Serving at the pleasure of the president
tulsi-gabbard.summary: The employment rule John Kiriakou says he was taught in his first week at the CIA: agency employees have none of the protections of the Civil Service Act and can be dismissed at will, over a bad tie or an unwelcome line in the President''s Daily Brief. He treats the rule as long-standing and harmless in itself, because every previous president wanted unbiased analysis — and as newly dangerous when a president fires the analysts whose assessments he dislikes.

tulsi-gabbard.title: Superdelegates
tulsi-gabbard.summary: The Democratic Party's automatic-delegate system, which John Kiriakou describes as created after George McGovern's 1972 landslide loss to return nominating power to party insiders. He cites West Virginia and Wyoming in 2016, where Bernie Sanders won the vote and Hillary Clinton took every delegate, and notes the Republican Party has no equivalent — which is why an insurgent like Donald Trump could win its nomination.

tulsi-gabbard.title: Bill Pulte
tulsi-gabbard.summary: The housing developer serving as acting Director of National Intelligence after Tulsi Gabbard's resignation. John Kiriakou, relaying the assessment of people who know him, calls him smart, personally decent and completely loyal to Trump — while saying he could not find the ODNI with a map and a GPS unit, and predicting his sole function will be to fire the president's enemies.

tulsi-gabbard.title: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
tulsi-gabbard.summary: The intelligence-community layer created in 2004, which John Kiriakou argues should never have existed. He traces its origin to George Tenet's failures over 9/11 and Iraq, notes it grew from sixteen employees to roughly twenty-four thousand, and points out that most agencies nominally under it are Defense Department bodies over which it controls nothing but the budget.

turning-point-usa.title: Charlie Kirk
turning-point-usa.summary: American conservative activist, founder of the movement John Kiriakou calls the centre of MAGA's youth vote, and — in the only meeting between them — a seventeen-year-old lobbyist Kiriakou watched run a Senate press conference and concluded was going places. Kiriakou disagreed with him on roughly eighty per cent of the issues, ranked his generational political impact alongside Martin Luther King and Robert F. Kennedy Sr., and notes that Kirk had turned against Israeli conduct in Gaza shortly before he was killed.

turning-point-usa.title: Charlie Kirk shooting
turning-point-usa.summary: Kiriakou questions the official account: a court filing says the ATF could not match the autopsy bullet to the rifle tied to the suspect.

turning-point-usa.title: ''An unusually violent society''
turning-point-usa.summary: The judgment the Amir of Bahrain delivered to John Kiriakou in the mid-1990s, shortly after the Oklahoma City bombing — that Americans are accepting of violence 'that would be unacceptable in any other civilized country,' even by Arab standards. Kiriakou says he had no answer, because it was true, and he has since used it as the frame for political shootings in the United States.

turning-point-usa.title: Candace Owens
turning-point-usa.summary: The commentator whose claims about the killing of Charlie Kirk John Kiriakou has publicly declined to accept. He credits her reach and her intelligence and rejects her method, citing an earlier occasion — a conference call he says he was on — at which she claimed irrefutable proof that the Italian government had stolen the 2020 election and that its release would return Donald Trump to office.

turning-point-usa.title: October 7 attack
turning-point-usa.summary: John Kiriakou's analysis of the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack as a policy failure, not an intelligence one — Israel was warned repeatedly, but Itamar Ben-Gvir diverted response forces to the West Bank, and Kiriakou believes Israel welcomed a pretext for overwhelming retaliation.

turning-point-usa.title: Senate Foreign Relations Committee
turning-point-usa.summary: Kiriakou was senior investigator under John Kerry — and still held the post when his own federal prosecution came to a head in January 2012.

twitter-state-affiliated-media-labels.title: Ed Schultz
twitter-state-affiliated-media-labels.summary: American broadcaster, a friend of John Kiriakou''s and later his colleague at RT, whom Kiriakou cites twice over: as a man forbidden by MSNBC to discuss Bernie Sanders during a primary, and as a dead man still being labelled a Russian government mouthpiece four years after his death.

twitter-state-affiliated-media-labels.title: The 2022 deplatforming
twitter-state-affiliated-media-labels.summary: The removal of John Kiriakou's radio programme from every major podcast platform after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, on the basis of his work for Sputnik News — preceded, he says, by a Washington Post article and a CSIS paper arguing that his weekly segment on American prison conditions was Russian propaganda weakening American democracy.

twitter-state-affiliated-media-labels.title: Kiriakou's daily news diet
twitter-state-affiliated-media-labels.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the wide range of mainstream and alternative outlets he reads each morning to compare competing angles, the two outlets — the Associated Press and ProPublica — he singles out as exceptional, and his broader habits of media consumption, from an admitted addiction to political polling to his distrust of AI chatbots after they repeatedly fabricated his own biography.

twitter-state-affiliated-media-labels.title: Kiriakou's Russian media work
twitter-state-affiliated-media-labels.summary: John Kiriakou's account of hosting a daily Sputnik radio show for seven and a half years with full contractual freedom to criticize anyone, including Putin — which he did on the morning of the Ukraine invasion — offered as a rebuttal to claims that Russian outlets are mere propaganda.

twitter-state-affiliated-media-labels.title: Panquake
twitter-state-affiliated-media-labels.summary: Open-source, blockchain-based social platform developed by the Iceland-registered company Talk Liberation, for which John Kiriakou has served as brand ambassador since 2020. Kiriakou describes it as advertising-free, subscription-funded, free of back doors, and run on servers powered by Icelandic geothermal steam — a project he frames as a David-and-Goliath fight against banks, big technology and governments.

twitter-state-affiliated-media-labels.title: Press TV website seizure
twitter-state-affiliated-media-labels.summary: The FBI's confiscation of the Press TV domain, which John Kiriakou cites alongside the banning of TeleSUR, RT and Sputnik as the point at which American censorship stopped being algorithmic and became straightforwardly physical.

two-abu-zubaydahs.title: Abu Zubaydah's diary
two-abu-zubaydahs.summary: The notebook captured with Abu Zubaydah, containing drawings and poetry, over which the CIA and the FBI came to deep disagreement — an FBI psychologist calling it the rantings of a crazy person and John Kiriakou insisting it showed creativity in a man who was not crazy at all.

two-abu-zubaydahs.title: The SpongeBob shirt
two-abu-zubaydahs.summary: The bright red SpongeBob SquarePants shirt, a Christmas present from his children, that John Kiriakou happened to be wearing when Abu Zubaydah opened his one good eye and realised the Americans had him.

two-abu-zubaydahs.title: The Syrian bodyguard
two-abu-zubaydahs.summary: The 330-pound guard captured alongside Abu Zubaydah, whose gunshot wound John Kiriakou examined and found ringed by a dinner-plate powder burn — evidence that contradicted the official account and left Kiriakou with a question about Pakistani intentions he says he will never be able to answer.

two-abu-zubaydahs.title: Abu Zubaydah
two-abu-zubaydahs.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

two-abu-zubaydahs.title: Buzzy Krongard
two-abu-zubaydahs.summary: The executive director of the CIA — the agency's third-ranking officer — who sat on the board of Johns Hopkins Medical Center and, on learning that Abu Zubaydah had been captured wounded, had the hospital's top trauma surgeon flown to Pakistan on a CIA jet.

two-party-system.title: Marjorie Taylor Greene
two-party-system.summary: American congresswoman whom John Kiriakou, despite deep political disagreement, has repeatedly credited for breaking with her party on the Epstein files, on military aid to Israel, and on Gaza. He describes her as courageous for pressing Donald Trump to release the files unredacted, and says the pressure ultimately forced her out of Washington.

two-party-system.title: ''An unusually violent society''
two-party-system.summary: The judgment the Amir of Bahrain delivered to John Kiriakou in the mid-1990s, shortly after the Oklahoma City bombing — that Americans are accepting of violence 'that would be unacceptable in any other civilized country,' even by Arab standards. Kiriakou says he had no answer, because it was true, and he has since used it as the frame for political shootings in the United States.

two-party-system.title: Candace Owens
two-party-system.summary: The commentator whose claims about the killing of Charlie Kirk John Kiriakou has publicly declined to accept. He credits her reach and her intelligence and rejects her method, citing an earlier occasion — a conference call he says he was on — at which she claimed irrefutable proof that the Italian government had stolen the 2020 election and that its release would return Donald Trump to office.

two-party-system.title: Tucker Carlson
two-party-system.summary: American broadcaster and former Fox News host; a personal friend of John Kiriakou's for years, appearing on Kiriakou's radio and podcast work and hosting him roughly a dozen times on his own Fox show. Kiriakou calls him possibly the most brilliant and best-informed person he has ever encountered, and relays Glenn Greenwald's belief that Carlson could win the presidency — an idea Carlson privately dismisses.

two-party-system.title: Charlie Kirk
two-party-system.summary: American conservative activist, founder of the movement John Kiriakou calls the centre of MAGA's youth vote, and — in the only meeting between them — a seventeen-year-old lobbyist Kiriakou watched run a Senate press conference and concluded was going places. Kiriakou disagreed with him on roughly eighty per cent of the issues, ranked his generational political impact alongside Martin Luther King and Robert F. Kennedy Sr., and notes that Kirk had turned against Israeli conduct in Gaza shortly before he was killed.

two-party-system.title: Democratic Party 2025 Political Snapshot
two-party-system.summary: John Kiriakou's 2025 assessment of Democratic Party weakness — a record-low 24% approval rating, seven Senate Democrats crossing over to hand Trump a spending-bill win with no concessions, and California governor Gavin Newsom's surprising denial of parole to a large group of long-incarcerated eligible inmates, which Kiriakou reads as Newsom "playing the long game."

tyrell-vanto.title: Jeff Fahey
tyrell-vanto.summary: American actor; star of the Tyrell Vanto film in which John Kiriakou made his acting debut in late 2025; characterized by Kiriakou as generous with his time and on-set advice.

tyrell-vanto.title: Erik Prince
tyrell-vanto.summary: Founder of Blackwater; CIA non-official-cover officer with a 201 file; identified publicly by Leon Panetta in front of the House Intelligence Committee; lives in Dubai outside U.S. jurisdiction; in popular culture invoked, alongside Elon Musk, as the composite figure for the billionaire in the Tyrell Vanto film featuring John Kiriakou.

tyrell-vanto.title: Hummus
tyrell-vanto.summary: The CIA's coercive 'rectal feeding' of detainees using pureed hummus — an unauthorized interrogation technique used at post-9/11 black sites, exposed in the 2014 Senate Torture Report, and the abuse for which John Kiriakou became most associated in popular culture.

tyrell-vanto.title: John Kiriakou
tyrell-vanto.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

tyrell-vanto.title: Lincoln's last turd
tyrell-vanto.summary: A purported piece of human waste attributed by a Pennsylvania circus-freak-show museum to Abraham Lincoln on the night of his assassination; auctioned for $5,000; subsequent DNA analysis disproved the attribution. John Kiriakou's failed bid for the artifact is the anecdote that, recirculated in early 2026, made him an internet meme figure.

uc-global-surveillance-of-assange.title: Brad Birkenfeld
uc-global-surveillance-of-assange.summary: The UBS banking whistleblower, who was prosecuted and imprisoned before winning a $104 million settlement from the Treasury Department and spending it on the legal defence of other whistleblowers. John Kiriakou uses him as the measure of the gap between financial and national-security whistleblowing, and names him among the visitors whose devices he believes were copied at the Ecuadorian embassy in London.

uc-global-surveillance-of-assange.title: Deep state
uc-global-surveillance-of-assange.summary: John Kiriakou''s position on the deep state — that it is not a right-wing trope but an accurate description of something he served inside for fifteen years at the CIA and two more on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee staff. He is indifferent to the label ("call it the state, call it the federal bureaucracy") and insists on the substance: "It''s there to stay. It''s not going anywhere."

uc-global-surveillance-of-assange.title: Julian Assange
uc-global-surveillance-of-assange.summary: Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.

uc-global-surveillance-of-assange.title: The Charles Littlejohn prosecution
uc-global-surveillance-of-assange.summary: The five-year sentence handed to an IRS contractor who disclosed Donald Trump's tax returns to the New York Times, which John Kiriakou calls stunning and unjustified — the material was protected but not classified, the Biden campaign made use of it, and the sentencing judge compared the disclosure to the January 6 attack on the Capitol.

uc-global-surveillance-of-assange.title: Joshua Schulte
uc-global-surveillance-of-assange.summary: Former CIA Directorate of Science and Technology engineer; source of the 2017 Vault 7 WikiLeaks disclosure of the agency's offensive technical capabilities; currently serving a 40-year federal sentence for espionage; maintains his innocence.

uc-global-surveillance-of-assange.title: The pillow talk leak case
uc-global-surveillance-of-assange.summary: A 1990s CIA disclosure John Kiriakou witnessed from the next desk: a colleague passed classified information to a retired senior officer she was involved with, who repeated it on CNN as a terrorism consultant. The agency traced it to her within days and punished her administratively — a letter in her file, two weeks without pay, a year without promotion. Kiriakou holds it up as the correct way to handle mishandled classified information.

uday-hussein.title: Saddam Hussein
uday-hussein.summary: President of Iraq from 1979 until the 2003 U.S. invasion; subject of John Kiriakou's CIA portfolio from January 1990 onward, in which capacity Kiriakou became, at age 25, "Saddam Hussein's intelligence community biographer" and the analyst who briefed President George H. W. Bush in the Oval Office on the morning of the 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

uday-hussein.title: Hussein Kamel
uday-hussein.summary: Saddam Hussein's son-in-law and Iraq's Minister of Industry and Military Industrialization; defected to Jordan in January 1993 with his brother Saddam Kamel out of fear of Uday Hussein; demanded U.S. weapons and air cover in exchange for cooperation but refused to disclose WMD locations; per John Kiriakou, the CIA burned him with a planted Arab-press leak that triggered Saddam to destroy his chemical-weapons stockpile.

uday-hussein.title: Ali Hassan al-Majid
uday-hussein.summary: Saddam Hussein cousin known as "Chemical Ali" and "the Butcher of Kurdistan"; per John Kiriakou, also briefly served as the Iraqi-installed governor of occupied Kuwait — "the Butcher of Kuwait" — and was engaged in the wholesale slaughter of Kurds in the north, Shia in the south, and Kuwaitis under occupation.

uday-hussein.title: Abu Zubaydah
uday-hussein.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

uday-hussein.title: Counterterrorism Center
uday-hussein.summary: The CIA's Counterterrorism Center (CTC) — the unit where John Kiriakou spent the defining years of his operational career. He joined in the late 1990s as the only officer in the entire CIA fluent in both Greek and Arabic, served as chief of counterintelligence in the bin Laden unit, watched the Center swell from a few hundred employees to nearly 2,000 by September 12, 2001, and it was to CTC that he walked back down in May 2002 to refuse the torture program — the moment, he says, the CIA began to turn on him.

uday-hussein.title: Office of Leadership Analysis
uday-hussein.summary: CIA analytic office — internally called LDA, for Leadership Development Analysis — founded by CIA psychiatrist Jerome Post, where John Kiriakou was hired at the start of his CIA career and spent his first seven and a half years as Saddam Hussein's classified psychological profiler. His first assignment, given on his first day, was covering Iraq and Kuwait, a portfolio his boss described as so quiet the office sometimes went days without a single incoming cable.

uk-secrecy-laws.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
uk-secrecy-laws.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

uk-secrecy-laws.title: BDS movement
uk-secrecy-laws.summary: The Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions movement against Israel; John Kiriakou notes that some 40 U.S. states now have anti-BDS laws that can require a speaker at a publicly funded university to sign a pledge of support for Israel — which he refuses to do.

uk-secrecy-laws.title: Andrew Bustamante
uk-secrecy-laws.summary: Former CIA officer who sells CIA-style training online; John Kiriakou identifies him as the lone critic of his work hosting a show on a Russian network, and argues Bustamante's training business — open to anyone who pays — is the more problematic of the two.

uk-secrecy-laws.title: China's base in Djibouti
uk-secrecy-laws.summary: Camp Lemonnier in Djibouti, the abandoned French base the Djiboutians offered to the Americans and the Chinese took a share of — split down the middle by a chain-link fence, the only Chinese military installation outside China, and the centrepiece of John Kiriakou's argument that China is not an expansionist power.

uk-secrecy-laws.title: China as economic threat
uk-secrecy-laws.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that China is the real threat to the West not militarily — it has one aircraft carrier to America's two dozen and rarely invades — but economically, buying friends worldwide while the U.S. spends a trillion dollars a year on weapons.

uk-secrecy-laws.title: Donald Trump
uk-secrecy-laws.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

ukraine-call-whistleblower.title: Presidential call memcons
ukraine-call-whistleblower.summary: How a call between the president and a foreign leader is staffed and recorded, as John Kiriakou describes it. Four people are usually on the line and rarely five — not the twenty reported during the Ukraine affair — and the write-up, a memorandum of conversation or memcon, is held so tightly inside the National Security Council that a CIA analyst, he says, would never see one.

ukraine-call-whistleblower.title: The Farm
ukraine-call-whistleblower.summary: The CIA's clandestine training facility in Virginia; site of approximately 80% of all CIA operational training

ukraine-call-whistleblower.title: Gina Haspel
ukraine-call-whistleblower.summary: Director of the Central Intelligence Agency under President Trump's first term; known to John Kiriakou and others at the CIA as "Bloody Gina"; per Kiriakou, flew out to the secret black site to sit in on one of the enhanced-interrogation torture sessions "just because she could," personally supervised the torture of USS Cole bombing suspect Rahim al-Nashiri, and later fed the CIA's torture tapes into an industrial document grinder after being explicitly told by White House Counsel not to destroy them.

ukraine-call-whistleblower.title: Scholar-in-Residence program
ukraine-call-whistleblower.summary: The current CIA recruitment program, in operation as of the late 2020s, under which the agency places retiring senior officers as 'CIA Scholar in Residence' professors at major American universities. Per John Kiriakou, the program serves as the agency's principal university-recruitment channel since the 1993 Equal Employment Opportunity Act forbade the older practice of having professors covertly recruit students into the CIA. Officers identified as scholars in residence are openly disclosed; the recruitment work continues, just no longer in secret.

ukraine-call-whistleblower.title: The 2007 death threats
ukraine-call-whistleblower.summary: The immediate personal consequence of John Kiriakou''s December 2007 television appearance confirming CIA waterboarding: hundreds of pieces of hate mail, and three threats against his life that the FBI classified as credible, one of which named his children and gave his home address. On the Bureau''s advice he took his family out of the country for a week; the FBI then interviewed the senders, judged them local cranks, and told him to come home.

ukraine-call-whistleblower.title: The 1996 campaign contribution disclosure
ukraine-call-whistleblower.summary: The whistleblower disclosure John Kiriakou made inside the CIA in 1996, sixteen years before the one that ruined him. Serving overseas, he learned of a very large illegal contribution to the Dole presidential campaign, reported it to the CIA Inspector General, and watched the system work exactly as written: the IG investigated, found the information credible, and referred it to the Federal Election Commission. He offers it as the control case against which he judges every later complaint.

ukraine-proxy-war.title: Major non-NATO ally status for Ukraine
ukraine-proxy-war.summary: John Kiriakou''s forecast of how the Russian demand that Ukraine never join NATO can be met without leaving Ukraine unprotected: the designation of major non-NATO ally, already held by Australia, Japan, South Korea, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, which he says confers essentially the same rights without the membership.

ukraine-proxy-war.title: China as mediator
ukraine-proxy-war.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that China is the plausible mediator of Middle Eastern and Ukrainian conflicts, grounded in his claim that — Tibet and its border wars aside — China has no history of invading other countries, and his observation of how quickly Beijing accepted an offhand suggestion that it might mediate between Israel and Iran.

ukraine-proxy-war.title: The CIA as a policy support agency
ukraine-proxy-war.summary: John Kiriakou''s standing correction to the idea that the CIA has a foreign policy of its own: it is not a policy agency but a policy support agency, it serves at the pleasure of the president, and its officers have no civil service protections at all. Career staff can slow-roll an order they dislike until an administration ends — but in a hot war, he says, they do as they are told.

ukraine-proxy-war.title: The KGB denial cables
ukraine-proxy-war.summary: Two occasions on which, according to John Kiriakou, the first message the CIA received after an American killing came from the KGB and said the same thing: we promise it wasn''t us. One followed the assassination of Athens station chief Richard Welch in December 1975, the other the killing of President Kennedy in November 1963. Kiriakou treats them as evidence of a standing gentleman''s agreement between the two services not to touch each other''s people — one he expects to hold even where Russian troops overrun CIA bases.

ukraine-proxy-war.title: Iran Nuclear Assessment
ukraine-proxy-war.summary: Per John Kiriakou's assessment, the US–Israeli military campaign against Iran was a war of choice driven by Israeli political pressure rather than genuine intelligence indicating an Iranian nuclear weapons threat. The CIA produced two National Intelligence Estimates concluding Iran had no nuclear weapons program; Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khamenei issued a fatwa in the 1980s forbidding such a program. The U.S. went to war anyway, in Kiriakou's view, after President Trump replaced the Joint Chiefs of Staff with officers willing to accept Israeli intelligence and proceed.

ukraine-proxy-war.title: Article 5, invoked once
ukraine-proxy-war.summary: John Kiriakou's argument against NATO's continued necessity, resting on the observation that in the alliance's whole history it has been called on to defend a member from attack exactly once — on 11 September 2001 — and on the repeated American promises to Russia not to expand toward its borders, which he says four presidents in a row have broken.

ukraine-settlement-prediction.title: Operation Spiderweb
ukraine-settlement-prediction.summary: The Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's strategic bomber fleet in June 2025, which John Kiriakou calls a brilliant operation and — against Volodymyr Zelensky's account — one Ukraine could not have run alone. Eighteen months of preparation, drones smuggled across eleven time zones by human couriers, and command from Kyiv all required outside help, he argues; and Donald Trump's uncharacteristic public silence afterwards is his evidence that Washington was in on it.

ukraine-settlement-prediction.title: Europe without Russian gas
ukraine-settlement-prediction.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that Europe needs Russia more than Russia needs Europe, made from what he has physically encountered rather than from figures. Speaking in Nottingham in 2025 he found the concert hall so cold that the audience complained, and was told by the manager that the venue could not afford to heat itself without Russian gas. He reports the same of homes in Britain, Germany and Greece, where American gas is simply too expensive to substitute.

ukraine-settlement-prediction.title: Ukraine as a proxy war
ukraine-settlement-prediction.summary: John Kiriakou's assessment, given two months into the 2022 Russian invasion, that the United States was funding a proxy war it knew Ukraine could not win in order to bog Russia down — and that the outcome was already fixed, so peace talks should happen at once.

ukraine-settlement-prediction.title: Volodymyr Zelensky
ukraine-settlement-prediction.summary: Kiriakou says he was told not to discuss Zelensky's corruption publicly, and calls the Oval Office dressing-down of him set up in advance.

ukraine-settlement-prediction.title: Vladimir Putin
ukraine-settlement-prediction.summary: President of Russia. Per John Kiriakou, Putin twice raised joining NATO — floating it to Bill Clinton and later telling Barack Obama Russia would like to explore membership — and was refused both times; Kiriakou has never believed Putin wants to conquer Ukraine or Eastern Europe, argues U.S. hostility toward Russia is driven by defense contractors and a permanent wartime economy, and notes the irony that Putin was the anti-communist the U.S. itself backed in the Yeltsin era.

ukraine-settlement-prediction.title: The Istanbul peace talks
